Earlier, Walmart officially announced that it will finally begin rolling out Apple Pay, after refusing to support it for more than ten years.

When will your local Walmart start supporting Apple Pay? I've got the full rollout timeline — here's everything you need to know...

Walmart Apple Pay Rollout Timeline

In an announcement today, Walmart said that Apple Pay and broader contactless payment support will begin rolling out next week, with full coverage across all U.S. stores expected by the end of this year.

According to an internal memo obtained by 9to5Mac that Walmart sent to store management today, the retailer provided a more detailed phased rollout plan. The company is currently planning to deploy state by state, in phases. Dates may shift if any issues arise during the rollout, but here's the current roadmap:

States Tap to Pay Launch Arkansas Aug. 24–31 California, Washington, Oregon, Nevada, Idaho, Alaska, Hawaii Sept. 10 Kansas, Louisiana, Nebraska, Oklahoma Sept. 14 Texas Sept. 17 Arizona, Utah, Colorado, New Mexico, South Dakota, Montana, North Dakota, Wyoming Sept. 21 Illinois, Ohio, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Iowa Sept. 24 Tennessee, Indiana, Michigan, Kentucky Sept. 28 Georgia, Alabama, Mississippi Oct. 1 Florida Oct. 5 North Carolina, Virginia, South Carolina, West Virginia, Puerto Rico Oct. 8 Pennsylvania, New York, New Jersey, Massachusetts, Maryland, Connecticut, New Hampshire, Maine, Delaware, Rhode Island, Vermont, District of Columbia Oct. 12

Currently, Missouri does not appear on Walmart's timeline, and the reason is unclear at this time.

In the memo, Walmart also listed all the contactless payment methods that will be supported:

  • Contactless-enabled credit and debit cards
  • Digital wallets, including Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Samsung Pay
  • Payment-enabled smartwatches and wearables
  • Supported contactless EBT cards

It's been a long time coming for Walmart to support Apple Pay. Will this change where you shop? Share your thoughts in the comments.
